newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MERRILL LYNCH CUTS BELGIAN KREDIETBANK.
newsitem.headline: MERRILL LYNCH CUTS BELGIAN KREDIETBANK.

text.p: Brokerage Merrill Lynch said on Wednesday it downgraded shares in Belgium's third largest bank Kredietbank to 'neutral' from 'accumulate' after the stock hit Merrill's price target.
"There was enough speculation in the share," Merrill's Belgian analyst said.
On a standalone basis, that is without merger or acquisition speculation, the share was worth 12,600 francs. With the benefits of an acquisition, its worth was 16,000 francs.
Kredietbank peaked at 16,200 francs on June 9 and was down 0.7 percent on a weaker Brussels bourse on Wednesday.

"Kredietbank had been trading at a 25 percent premium to its fair value," the analyst said. "We do believe the bank will do an acquisition and benefits of that, cost savings and such, should translate into a share price of 16,000 francs."
He added that currently there was not enough speculation "to keep Kredietbank as an 'accumulate'."

A 'neutral' rating by Merrill's means the share is expected to move in a plus 10 percent/minus 10 percent range around current levels. 'Accumulate' sets a target of plus 10 to plus 20 percent for the share.
The Merrill analyst said those who wanted to "play" the possibility of a major reshaping of the Belgian banking scene should focus on Almanij , the holding company behind Kredietbank.
Kredietbank shares were down 50 francs at 14,700 at 1030 GMT. Almanij was up 100 francs at 16,500.
